
=================================================================
#54 Talhae  (-19)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: founder fairy tale, con-man comedy
Logline: A chest washes in on the tide with a magpie crying over it. What climbs out is a con man.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Late in the first king’s reign, a chest comes in on the tide at a fishing beach. A magpie flies over it, crying.
[1] ¶ It has come a long way. A thousand li north-east of Wa, the islands across the sea, the queen of a country called Dapana carried a child for seven years and was delivered of an egg. The king said a person who lays an egg is an ill omen and should get rid of it. She could not. She wrapped it in silk, packed it in a chest with treasure, and gave it to the sea.
[2] ¶ It reaches Gaya first. The people of Golden Gaya see a strange chest bobbing off their beach and, being sensible, leave it there.
[3] ¶ Gaya tells it differently, and with more nerve. In the Gaya chronicle Talhae comes ashore a grown man, walks into King Suro’s hall, and asks for the throne.
[4] [CARD Seok Talhae: Seok Talhae. He arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach.]
[5] Seok Talhae: I’ve come for your throne. / You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon.
[6] King Suro: …Heaven gave it to me. / I— it isn’t mine to give. Or to… lose.
[7] ¶ So they fight the way kings fight in that country. Talhae becomes a hawk, and Suro becomes an eagle. Talhae becomes a sparrow, and Suro becomes a falcon. When Talhae is a man again he is standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders, and he bows.
[8] Seok Talhae: …That was a falcon. / Fine. I’ll find a country with a smaller king.
[9] ── SCENE: Ajinpo ──
[10] ¶ Either way, the chest goes on. At Ajinpo an old woman on the shore hauls it in with a rope and opens it, and there is a little boy inside, sitting among the treasure as if it were his luggage.
[11] 👵: Well. / You’re not a fish.
[12] Seok Talhae: No. / Is this the country?
[13] ¶ She names him herself, since there is nobody else to ask. A magpie followed the chest in, so she takes the bird out of the character for magpie, and what is left, **Seok**, is his surname. He got loose from the chest and came out of it, so he is **Talhae**, the one who got loose.
[14] ¶ He grows nine cheok tall, fishes to feed the old woman and never once complains about it, and when she tells him that a boy with bones like his should study, he studies geography. Mostly the part about where the good ground is.
[15] ── SCENE: The Crescent House ──
[16] ¶ Looking over the city, he picks the best ground in it, a crescent-shaped rise above the river, and finds that someone already lives there. The house belongs to **Hogong**, a minister who came over the sea from Wa long ago with a gourd tied at his waist to float on, and has the name to prove it.
[17] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Hyeokgeose, yr. 38): As for Hogong, his clan and surname are not known. He was a man of Wa, and at first he crossed the sea with a gourd tied at his waist; hence he was called Hogong, Lord Gourd.❞
[18] ¶ Talhae does not have a house. He has a plan. One night he buries a whetstone and a sack of charcoal beside Hogong’s gate, and in the morning he goes to the magistrate and says the house was his family’s, taken while they were away.
[19] Hogong: I have lived in that house thirty years!
[20] Seok Talhae: And my family lived there before you. We were smiths. / Dig by the gate, if you don’t believe me.
[21] ¶ They dig. The whetstone and the charcoal come up out of the ground, black and convincing, and the magistrate gives Talhae the house.
[22] Hogong: …You buried those last night.
[23] Seok Talhae: Prove it.
[24] ¶ The ground becomes **the Moon Palace**, where every king of Silla after him will live, which means every king of Silla lives in a stolen house, including the one who has just moved in. Nobody in the palace likes it when you mention this.
[25] ── SCENE: Two Kings Later ──
[26] ¶ King Namhae hears about the clever young man in the crescent house and marries him to his daughter. Two kings later Talhae is sixty-two and on the throne himself, and one of the first things he does is make Hogong his chief minister, which is either an apology or the best joke in the annals.
[27] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum): Second year, spring, first month: he appointed Hogong Grand Minister.❞
[28] Hogong: …Grand Minister.
[29] Seok Talhae: You know the best ground in the city. I could use a man like that.
[30] Hogong: I knew it. You did bury them.
[31] Seok Talhae: Prove it.
[32] ── SCENE: The Moon Palace ──
[33] ¶ Seven hundred years later, King Muyeol spends his first night in the stolen house awake. He keeps listening for someone digging by the gate.
[34] Munhee: Nobody is digging, Your Majesty. Go to sleep. / And if a rooster crows, it’s a rooster.
[35] ¶ **“Hogong. There’s a rooster in the woods.” It is the middle of the night. Roosters don’t crow at night…!**
